name: Fault-equivalent six-legged spider
summary: A phase-free six-legged Z-spider is fault-equivalent to a triangle of three Z-spiders with two legs each.
description:
A six-legged Z-spider can be replaced by a triangle of three Z-spiders, each carrying two of the legs. Like the [four-legged](../fe-four-legged-spider/) and [five-legged](../fe-five-legged-spider/) rules it decomposes a spider into a ring, which forms a detecting region for the flips on its internal edges. Fault equivalence is with respect to *edge-flip noise*: every edge of the diagram can suffer a Pauli $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ flip of weight 1.

In Schweikart's thesis the rule is shown to be moreover *matchability-preserving* in a blossom-shaped detector context: the rewritten diagram keeps a detector basis in which every fault triggers at most two detectors, so that it can still be decoded by minimum-weight perfect matching.
